neighbours.label: an adjective of large size or importance before its noun (' major', ' large', also ' big', ' significant', ' huge'), often after a count ('two large groupings', 'the last major storm'); the other side of the distinction is small: quiet on ' small'/' minor', and the output suppresses ' small'
fire: The delta is divided into three large islands and a maze of channels.
The earthquake was the first major disaster the young government had faced.
The museum owns two large collections of medieval coins.
The treaty ended the last major conflict between the two kingdoms.
The valley floor is crossed by four big rivers flowing north.
Engineers found one major flaw in the design of the dam.
The estate was split into five large farms after the war.
The audit uncovered several significant errors in the accounts.
quiet: The delta is divided into three small islands and a maze of channels.
The earthquake was the first minor tremor the young government had faced.
The museum owns two tiny collections of medieval coins.
The treaty ended the last naval conflict between the two kingdoms.
The valley floor is crossed by four shallow rivers flowing north.
Engineers found one hidden flaw in the design of the dam.
The estate was split into five little farms after the war.
The audit uncovered several amusing errors in the accounts.

notes: Card: ' major' x13, ' large' x8. Probes: major 0.59, large 0.57, big 0.36, significant 0.30, huge 0.23; small 0.00, minor 0.01, 'great achievement' 0.00. Near misses keep the frame and swap in small/minor or a non-size adjective.
